events.what: Zheglov preprint claiming the Dixmier conjecture for the first Weyl algebra (n=1)
Explicit polynomial self-map of C^3 with constant Jacobian -2 that is not injective, refuting JC_3 and hence (via the known implication DC_n => JC_n) the Dixmier conjecture for A_n, n>=3
events.ai_basis: hello there the jacobian conjecture is false thanx to my close friend akhil for asking about it and my other close friend fable for working during the world cup final

judgement.doubts: The bullet asserts that ANY endomorphism of A Weyl algebra is an automorphism — a universal statement over all n — so a counterexample in A_3 refutes it as worded; the record itself calls n>=3 'a case' but that reading treats the bullet as DC_1 or as per-n questions, which its words do not. The Dixmier counterexample is obtained from the Jacobian map by the standard easy-direction construction (x_i -> F_i, derivations via the polynomial inverse Jacobian), which is explicit given constant Jacobian; the map itself is checkable and digested by Tao. Readers who take 'the Dixmier conjecture' to mean DC_1 would call it still open (Zheglov's claim unreviewed). AI role 'generated' rests on a thin primary quote plus secondary glosses; 'assisted' is plausible.

corrections.why: F3/F2 reverse: the bullet says 'any endomorphism of a Weyl algebra is an automorphism', a single universal claim; the record's own outcome states the JC_3 counterexample 'falsifies the Dixmier conjecture for the n-th Weyl algebra for every n≥3', which refutes the bullet as worded. The map is explicit, computer-algebra checkable and digested by Tao (terrytao.wordpress.com 2026-07-21), so whole + digested/checkable = resolved (refuted).

F9: kept, but Alpöge's quote ('fable for working during the world cup final') does not say the model produced the map; 'generated' rests on secondary sources saying Fable found it, and the record's competing_reading notes 'assisted' fits equally well.
